titulo: Setup: flag, origin trial, polyfill, and three test modes
lead: You don't need an experimental Chrome installed to work. The kit serves the page on a local server and opens the same Playwright Chromium in three modes: without the API, with the polyfill, and with native WebMCP behind the test flag. No cost and no API key.
objetivo: set up the kit and see the same page in three modes (no API, polyfill, native) without spending quota or installing an experimental Chrome.

aprende.t: Clone the kit and install it with pinned versions
Secure context: https in production, 127.0.0.1 for rehearsal
The three modes: sem, polyfill, and nativo
Origin trial and flag in your Chrome, when you want to see it live

hero_alt: Dark workbench with an open laptop showing a browser, a physical switch turned on, and a network cable plugged in.

nos.detalhe: Chromium without the flag: document.modelContext does not exist. This is the ordinary visitor (Safari, Firefox, stable Chrome). The page must work the same through the form.

The page loads @mcp-b/webmcp-polyfill 6.0.3 with ?ensaio=polyfill. It is a temporary redistribution of the CG's own polyfill, maintained by MCP-B: unofficial and, in the package's own words, "will eventually be removed". It does not fire toolactivated or toolcancel.

Playwright 1.64.0's Chromium 156.0.8078.4 with --enable-features=WebMCPTesting, the same as the chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing flag. It is Chrome's own implementation, with no token and no Canary. Experimental as of 10/19/2026.
On your domain, with an origin trial token (Chrome 149–156) in a meta tag or header. Only people using Chrome or Edge in the trial see the tools; everyone else falls back to the No API mode.

secoes.legenda: Always test the No API mode: it is what most visitors see.
secoes.dica: The API only exists in a secure context: https or localhost/127.0.0.1. That is why the kit serves the page at 127.0.0.1.

secoes.sub: Versions pinned on 10/19/2026: @mcp-b/webmcp-polyfill 6.0.3 and playwright 1.64.0. The postinstall copies the polyfill to pagina/vendor/ (for rehearsal only).

blocos.rot: Terminal · clone, install, and download Chromium
blocos.conteudo:
git clone -q https://github.com/inematds/formacao-webmcp-site-v72 ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-site-v72
cd ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-site-v72/kit
npm ci
npx playwright install chromium
echo "saída: $?"

secoes.titulo: What the page sees in each mode
secoes.sub: ambiente.mjs opens the page in the three modes and reads: secure context, document.modelContext, the old name navigator.modelContext, and the on-screen notice.

abas.html:
== Chromium 156.0.8078.4 (Playwright) · modo: sem
contexto seguro: sim · document.modelContext: ausente · navigator.modelContext: ausente
página: sem · aviso: Este navegador não expõe WebMCP. Tudo funciona pelo formulário.
== Chromium 156.0.8078.4 (Playwright) · modo: polyfill
contexto seguro: sim · document.modelContext: presente · navigator.modelContext: ausente
página: com · aviso: WebMCP ativo: 4 ferramentas registradas.
== Chromium 156.0.8078.4 (Playwright) · modo: nativo
contexto seguro: sim · document.modelContext: presente · navigator.modelContext: ausente
página: com · aviso: WebMCP ativo: 4 ferramentas registradas.
saída: 0

In the No API mode, the page shows a notice and carries on through the form. In the other two, it registers 4 tools. In none of them does navigator.modelContext exist.

secoes.sub: Experimental as of 10/19/2026. Nothing here is a done-when criterion.

texto: Open chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing, turn it on, and restart Chrome.
Run the kit's server and open the URL it prints.
Without the flag, add ?ensaio=polyfill to the URL.
The page loads the polyfill from pagina/vendor/ and registers the same tools.
Google publishes the Model Context Tool Inspector extension, which lists the tools and calls them in natural language.
It asks for an API key for a model (Gemini). It is not needed in this course.
Register your domain in the WebMCP origin trial and paste the token into the meta tag at the top of kit/pagina/index.html.
The token is registered for the site's domain; on localhost, use the flag.

secoes.sub: All local, no cost. Each exercise ends with a done when.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Why does the kit serve the page at 127.0.0.1 instead of opening the file directly?
opcoes: Because Playwright can't open a local file by its disk path.
Because the polyfill only works with Node.
Because the API requires a secure context, and 127.0.0.1 counts as secure.
Because the origin trial only accepts an IP address.
perguntas.explica: ModelContext is [SecureContext]: it only exists on https or localhost/127.0.0.1. In production, https. The common mistake is testing through file:// and thinking the API disappeared.

opcoes: That the page works for people who don't have the API.
That the polyfill was loaded correctly before the tools were registered.
That the origin trial token is valid.
That the agent picks the right tool.
perguntas.explica: "Sem" is the ordinary visitor. If the page breaks there, it broke for most people. The other modes prove the agent's path.

opcoes: The official W3C implementation for production.
A Chrome plugin that turns on the test flag by itself, without you opening chrome://flags.
A bridge that connects the page to Claude Desktop.
An unofficial, temporary rehearsal of the spec's API.
perguntas.explica: It is a temporary redistribution of the CG's polyfill, maintained by MCP-B, and it warns that it will be removed. It is for rehearsing the spec's API; it does not fire toolactivated/toolcancel. The bridge to MCP is @mcp-b/global, outside this course.

perguntas.p: Which mode uses Chrome's real implementation without a token?
opcoes: The "nativo" mode, Playwright's Chromium with the test flag.
Polyfill mode, with ?ensaio=polyfill at the end of the kit page's address.
None: without a token there is no implementation.
perguntas.explica: Playwright 1.64.0's Chromium 156.0.8078.4 with --enable-features=WebMCPTesting exposes Chrome's implementation. It is experimental and may change until the end of the trial (156).

itens.texto: One clone, npm ci and Playwright's Chromium: no experimental Chrome installed.
No API tests the fallback, Polyfill rehearses the API, Native runs Chrome's implementation.
Origin trial on your domain; the rest of your visitors fall back to the No API mode.
